title: Collector lease manager and tenant quarantine for private/dedicated observability
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description: Background: Dedicated and Private customers run site-local collectors and perimeter forwarders that ingest traces, metrics, and logs. We've observed noisy-tenant cases where a tenant's misconfigured SDK or replay floods a collector, degrading latency for other tenants and causing missed tracing spans. Goal: implement a Collector Lease Manager (CLM) that assigns time-limited leases to tenant streams on shared collectors, and a Tenant Quarantine flow to isolate and (optionally) replay suspicious streams to a separate sandbox pipeline. The CLM should integrate with tracing hooks to mark leases in span attributes and emit metrics for lease churn, preemption, and quarantine events.
acceptance_criteria: CLM assigns leases per-tenant-shard with configurable TTL and renewal policy
Collectors enforce a soft limit per-lease and emit lease_backpressure metrics when exceeded
Tenant Quarantine triggers after three consecutive lease violations in a rolling window; quarantined traffic is routed to a sandbox pipeline and flagged in traces
All control-plane decisions are logged and available in the console UI under Private Observability > Collector Leases
End-to-end test that simulates noisy tenant and verifies isolation without impacting healthy tenants' latency by >99%
Security review completed for lease-control RPCs and quarantine replay access
implementation_notes: Lease coordinator will be implemented as a small control-plane service colocated in per-region control-plane for Private deployments
Collector agents will expose lease-manager client with gRPC and switch to ephemeral in-memory queues for quarantined tenants
Lease ttl default = 15s, renewal slop = 5s; configuration surfaced via per-deployment YAML
Backpressure signal: collectors increment 'collector.lease.backpressure' counter and add span.attr 'collector.quarantine_suspected'
Sandbox pipeline retains quarantined tenant data for 48h by default and exposes a replay endpoint guarded by RBAC
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Alternative: full tenant siloing (dedicated collector per tenant) avoids complexity but is cost-prohibitive for mid-sized customers
Alternative: rate-limiting at edge probes reduces collector load but loses fidelity for tracing and aggregation
Chosen: lease-based approach gives graceful degradation, fine-grained metrics, and replay capability while keeping operational costs reasonable
